results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 58 aligned outline summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order; the three callout entries match no paragraph (they carry the KEY POINTS / IN THIS CHAPTER placements declared in introduction.thesis_statement and roadmap).
Every outline summary agrees with its aligned spec paragraph (p01-p56, including the moved p11/p10, p15a, p18a, p37a, p39, p41, p38 positions); no unit is missing, extra or out of order.

Only Index as a Copy ¶14 was marked two_ideas (reindexing embeddings / vendor uplift claims lack controls). Spec p24 declares exactly this paragraph as "two cautions" applying to AI retrieval, one counterargument; the unit opens with "Two cautions." and holds to it. No other unit was marked.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim through its section advances_thesis: scene to S2/S3, three ways to S1/S2, index as a copy to S3-S5, reviews to S6, choices to S2/S5, stages to S4, in practice to S2/S4, failures to S4-S6, conclusion to the thesis. The Amazon history in ¶12 traces to S5 (test against a baseline before buying), though readers found it a detour (recorded under flow).

Each table, figure, source and quotation is followed or framed by a sentence saying what it shows: the scene table ("The report made three things visible"), the three-ways table, Baymard ("Sites handle the product name and fail the words shoppers actually use"), Figure 2, the facts table ("Behind the table is..."), the interaction table, Elasticsearch synonyms, Algolia rules, Shopify facet limits (the half-filled waterproof facet), Amazon (the baseline lesson), the vector quotation, the Algolia/Constructor lifts ("Present them as 'the vendor reports'"), the B2B designs, the directive and FTC rule, the choices table ("The first two rows carry the difference"), the stages table, vendor limits and metrics, commercetools retirement. One reader reports the stages sentence disagrees with the table on where events belong (recorded under flow, uncorroborated).

Declared example relationship carrying over "the rule that a fact no feed can keep fresh enough is fetched at query time". The preceding unit ends on three numbered conditions; the only thing it calls a "rule" is the pricing chapter's rule for copies, so "that rule" points at the wrong antecedent and the third condition is not picked up by name. Flow reader 2 (item 5) stumbled on exactly this.

results.finding: The introduction opens with the declared intriguing example (the jacket whose rating lives in a spreadsheet) and states the premise; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, "dawn of man" or book report.

The conclusion does not open with "in conclusion", does not merely restate the thesis, adds no new subtopic and holds no body evidence beyond the source attributions in the Established list; it is none of the four weak types.

What to Take Away ¶1 states what no section states (the jacket, the stale "in stock", the overstaying rule and the orphaned review are one fault: a results page showing what its sources do not support, owned outside search) and says why it matters (fund attributes and a stock feed before a vendor). The supporting figure for the so-what is flawed (recorded under flow_is_followable, fault spec).

"The chapter opened with a waterproof jacket that search could not find because its rating lived in a spreadsheet" returns to the hook, and the paragraph says why no ranking algorithm could have found it and what does (a synonym, then the attribute from Q3 2027), as callback.how requires.

The intro-only reader predicts the sections in order (scene, vocabulary and three ways, index as a copy with feeds, ranking, filters, AI retrieval and wholesale, reviews, comparison by scale stage and vendor documentation, failures with detection and recovery), the evidence (Kestrel & Pine report, vendor documentation, EU/US review rules) and the tone. Only the usability research is not predicted; minor.

The reader names a data gap (words not in indexed fields, the rating in a spreadsheet, missing per-language synonyms, unindexed product) and checks zero-result rate and top failing queries per language and which fields are indexed before any new engine, citing 9.4% to 4.1% on the same engine. Matches expected.

The reader answers: only a coarse "available" flag in the index for filtering, exact figure from the availability service at query time; an indexed fact is only as fresh as the last run and stock changes by the second (the two-hour Phantom Stock). Matches expected.

The reader answers: how the review was collected and the linked order, kept in the merchant's own store, because Directive 2019/2161 makes real-purchaser status material and blacklists the claim without reasonable steps to check; also the FTC rule. Matches expected.
